content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering Pseudo-classes (:hover, :focus, :active, :visited) in Tailwind CSS"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Pseudo-classes allow you to apply styles to elements based on their state, such as when a user hovers over a button, focuses on an input field, clicks an element, or has previously visited a link. In Tailwind CSS, state variants are prefixed to utility classes using a colon (e.g., hover:bg-blue-600)."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. The Hover State (:hover)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The hover pseudo-class is triggered when the user places the cursor over an element. It is commonly used for buttons, links, and card components to provide visual feedback."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":""},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. The Focus State (:focus)"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"The focus pseudo-class applies when an element receives keyboard focus or is clicked. This is especially important for form inputs, textareas, and accessibility compliance."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":""},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. The Active State (:active)"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"The active pseudo-class is applied during the exact moment an element is being interacted with (e.g., the moment a mouse button is pressed down on a button)."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":""},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"4. The Visited State (:visited)"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"The visited pseudo-class styles links that the user has already visited. Due to privacy restrictions in modern browsers, you are limited in what styles you can apply (usually color and border-color)."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":" Example Link "},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Combining Multiple States"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can chain multiple pseudo-class prefixes together to create rich, interactive components that respond to various user actions seamlessly."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":""},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always combine pseudo-classes like focus with focus:outline-none and a custom ring to maintain strong accessibility."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use the transition utility class to make state changes smooth instead of abrupt."}]
